title: BFAR Vessel BRP Datu Magat Salamat Runs Aground at Hasa-Hasa (Half Moon) Shoal During Fuel Subsidy Mission, Refloated by PCG
detail: The Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources vessel BRP Datu Magat Salamat ran aground in the shallow waters of Hasa-Hasa (Half Moon) Shoal on September 17, 2026 while approaching a cluster of 15 to 20 Filipino fishing bancas to distribute fuel subsidies under the government's Kaagapay ng Bawat Mangingisda (KBBM) program. The fishing boats tried to tow the grounded vessel free but failed due to the morning low tide and their limited pulling power. The Philippine Coast Guard dispatched BRP Malabrigo from Buliluyan Port in Bataraza, Palawan, which arrived around noon, laid out a 600-meter towing line, and pulled the BFAR vessel free at approximately 3:34 p.m. No Chinese forces were involved in the grounding; the incident preceded by one day a China Coast Guard ramming of the same vessel near Abad Santos Shoal on September 18.

title: Maritime Advocacy Group Flags Two PLA Navy Survey Ships Near Galoc Island and Panatag Shoal; Palace Says PCG Verifying
detail: Alyansa ng Bantay sa Kapayapaan at Demokrasya (ABKD) Chairman Emeritus Jose Antonio Goitia warned on September 17, 2026 that two Chinese People's Liberation Army Navy Type 636A hydrographic survey ships — Hai Yang 23 Hao (pennant 873, ex-Qian Xuesen) and Hai Yang 24 Hao (pennant 874, ex-Deng Jiaxian) — were detected on September 11 operating inside Philippine waters: Hai Yang 23 roughly 1.15 nautical miles south of Galoc Island off northwest Palawan, and Hai Yang 24 about 64.28 nautical miles west-northwest of Panatag Shoal (Bajo de Masinloc/Scarborough Shoal). Goitia said 'these are not ordinary research vessels. They are military survey ships capable of collecting detailed information about our maritime environment,' and flagged their proximity to submarine cable infrastructure that carries roughly 99% of global internet traffic, saying 'seabed data can be used for scientific research, but it can also assist with naval navigation and submarine operations.' He called on authorities to 'track them, document their activities and defend our rights,' and cited Republic Act No. 12065, which bars foreign vessels from conducting hydrographic or oceanographic surveys in Philippine waters without prior authorization. Presidential Communications Office Undersecretary Claire Castro said the Philippine Coast Guard was still verifying the report, adding the government could not yet characterize China's intentions because 'the PCG is still verifying such report.'

media.caption: One of the two Chinese PLA Navy Type 636A hydrographic survey ships flagged near Galoc Island and Panatag Shoal
